title: Laser Guide Star at the VLT
caption: A laser guide star beam against the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The soft glow of the Milky Way is cut through by a stark orange beam shooting up from one of the Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope. ESO calls the VLT a premier observing facility; it stands at the Paranal Observatory in northern Chile.

The beam belongs to a Laser Guide Star. It lights up a small artificial point high in the atmosphere, which the telescope can use as a reference. Systems known as adaptive optics watch how that point shimmers and use the information to undo the blurring that Earth's turbulent air adds to every image.

Behind the beam lies our galaxy, seen from within as a pale band. Put together, the scene sets two kinds of light side by side: the soft glow of countless distant stars, and a bright, human-made line aimed at helping telescopes see them more sharply.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way appears brighter here than it would to someone standing near the telescope.

explore: The beam comes from one of the Unit Telescopes that make up ESO's Very Large Telescope. The stark orange colour of the laser contrasts with the soft, familiar glow of the Milky Way behind it.
alt: An orange laser beam rising from a telescope enclosure across the soft glow of the Milky Way.
